intro.data: You can package results two ways: a List (any number of items) or an Optional (one item, or none). safeHead pulls a single result out of a List — the first item, or nothing if the list is empty. The point of this chapter: that one rule must work the SAME way for every kind of content — a list of Users, a list of Emails, anything. On the left are the content types; for each, pick the safeHead converter.
intro.alchemy: You can store a reagent two ways: a rack of vials (any number) or a single vial, which may be empty. 'Take First' draws one result from a rack — the first vial, or nothing if the rack is bare. The point of this chapter: that one method must work the SAME way for every reagent — a rack of Herbs, a rack of Essences, anything. On the left are the reagents; for each, pick the 'Take First' method.
intro.spellcraft: You can hold an essence two ways: a stack of runes (any number) or a single rune, or none at all. 'Take Top' draws one result from a stack — the top rune, or nothing if the stack is empty. The point of this chapter: that one working must read the SAME way for every essence — a stack of Runes, a stack of Sparks, anything. On the left are the essences; for each, pick the 'Take Top' working.
intro.abstract: Two functors F, G : C → D are given. A natural transformation α : F ⇒ G is a single arrow between them: a component α_A : F(A) → G(A) at every object A. Choose the component at each object.

goal.data: Pick the safeHead converter for both the User list and the Email list.
goal.alchemy: Pick the 'Take First' method for both the Herb rack and the Essence rack.
goal.spellcraft: Choose the 'Take Top' working for both the Rune stack and the Spark stack.
goal.abstract: At each object, choose the component α_A : F(A) → G(A).

afterSuccess.data: You picked safeHead for every content type — one rule that pulls the first item out of any List the same way everywhere. That single, uniform rule is what we call a natural transformation.
afterSuccess.alchemy: You picked 'Take First' for every reagent — one method that draws the first vial from any rack the same way everywhere. That single, uniform rule is what we call a natural transformation.

afterSuccess.abstract: You chose a component at every object — together they form a natural transformation α : F ⇒ G.

reveal.summary: A natural transformation α : F ⇒ G is a family of components α_A : F(A) → G(A), one for every object A — a single arrow between two functors.
reveal.moreFormal: The components must satisfy the naturality condition (next puzzle). Natural transformations are the morphisms of the functor category [C, D]; functors are its objects.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: safeHead<A>: List<A> => Optional<A> — one polymorphic function, all types at once.
